policy_name: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449)
country_region: OECD members and adherent non-member countries
geo_constraints: Adherents (OECD members and non-members that adhered); addressed to governments and, via governments, all AI actors

key_dates.event: Adopted by the OECD Council at Ministerial level
G20 AI Principles drawing on the OECD Principles welcomed (date from general knowledge; not verified)
Council revises the definition of 'AI system' (date from general knowledge; not verified on official host)
Council adopts revised Recommendation (updated principles incl. safety, information integrity, rule of law)

covered_entities: AI actors (those who play an active role in the AI system lifecycle)
covered_activities: national AI policies and international cooperation
objective: Foster innovation and trust in AI by promoting responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI that respects human rights and democratic values, and set recommendations for national policies and international cooperation.
principles: inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being
respect for the rule of law, human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy
conflict_rule: Non-binding soft law; no conflict rule. Adherents implement through domestic measures.

record_provenance.notes: OECD hosts were blocked; adoption (2019-05-22) and revision (2024-05-03) dates are from well-established knowledge, not re-verified. Number of adherents changes over time and is not recorded. Clause texts reflect the 2024 revised wording as recalled; not verbatim-verified.

clauses.section: Principle 1.2 (Respect for the rule of law, human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy)
clauses.original_text: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights, democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI system lifecycle. These include non-discrimination and equality, freedom, dignity, autonomy of individuals, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice, and internationally recognised labour rights. … To this end, AI actors should implement mechanisms and safeguards, such as capacity for human agency and oversight, including to address risks arising from uses outside of intended purpose, intentional misuse, or unintentional misuse in a manner appropriate to the context and consistent with the state of the art.
clauses.requirement: respect rule of law, human rights and democratic values; implement human agency and oversight safeguards
clauses.interpretation_notes: Not verbatim-verified: the official host (legalinstruments.oecd.org) was not reachable from the compilation environment (network policy), so this wording is the compiler's reconstruction of the official text and must be checked against the official source before being treated as a quotation.

clauses.original_text: AI Actors should commit to transparency and responsible disclosure regarding AI systems. To this end, they should provide meaningful information, appropriate to the context, and consistent with the state of art: … to make stakeholders aware of their interactions with AI systems, including in the workplace, … where feasible and useful, to provide plain and easy-to-understand information on the sources of data/input, factors, processes and/or logic that led to the prediction, content, recommendation or decision, to enable those affected by an AI system to understand the output, and, to provide information that enable those adversely affected by an AI system to challenge its output.
clauses.requirement: disclose AI interactions and explain outputs to enable understanding and challenge
clauses.condition: appropriate to context and consistent with state of the art; where feasible and useful
clauses.affected_asset: affected persons' ability to understand and challenge AI outputs
clauses.interpretation_notes: Not verbatim-verified: the official host (legalinstruments.oecd.org) was not reachable from the compilation environment (network policy), so this wording is the compiler's reconstruction of the official text and must be checked against the official source before being treated as a quotation.

clauses.original_text: a) AI systems should be robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle so that, in conditions of normal use, foreseeable use or misuse, or other adverse conditions, they function appropriately and do not pose unreasonable safety and/or security risks. b) Mechanisms should be in place, as appropriate, to ensure that if AI systems risk causing undue harm or exhibit undesired behaviour, they can be overridden, repaired, and/or decommissioned safely as needed. c) Mechanisms should also, where technically feasible, be in place to bolster information integrity while ensuring respect for freedom of expression.
clauses.requirement: ensure robustness, security and safety; enable safe override, repair or decommissioning; bolster information integrity
clauses.condition: throughout lifecycle, incl. normal use, foreseeable use or misuse
clauses.purpose: prevent unreasonable safety/security risks and undue harm
clauses.affected_asset: safety and security of people; information integrity
clauses.interpretation_notes: Not verbatim-verified: the official host (legalinstruments.oecd.org) was not reachable from the compilation environment (network policy), so this wording is the compiler's reconstruction of the official text and must be checked against the official source before being treated as a quotation. Points (b) and (c) were added in the 2024 revision.

clauses.original_text: AI actors should be accountable for the proper functioning of AI systems and for the respect of the above principles, based on their roles, the context, and consistent with the state of the art. … AI actors should, based on their roles, the context, and their ability to act, apply a systematic risk management approach to each phase of the AI system lifecycle on an ongoing basis and adopt responsible business conduct to address risks related to AI systems, …
clauses.action: be accountable; apply systematic risk management
clauses.requirement: be accountable and apply systematic, ongoing lifecycle risk management
clauses.condition: based on roles, context and ability to act
